canonical_claim: Given an infinite structure M for a first-order language L and every infinite cardinal kappa at least as large as both the language and M, there is an L-structure N of cardinality kappa that is elementarily equivalent to M.
source_phrase: 无穷模型有任意大的初等等价模型

canonical_formal_target.environment_fingerprint: Lean 4.29.0 commit 98dc76e3c0a9b856c9b98726b713fb04fab16740; mathlib 8a178386ffc0f5fef0b77738bb5449d50efeea95; import Mathlib.ModelTheory.Satisfiability; pp.explicit=true; pp.universes=true

domain_and_universes: L : FirstOrder.Language.{u,v}; M : Type w' with L.Structure M; kappa : Cardinal.{w}; N : CategoryTheory.Bundled L.Structure in universe w. All cross-universe cardinal comparisons use the lifts printed in statement-elaboration.txt.
quantifiers: L, M, the L.Structure M instance, Infinite M, kappa, aleph_0 <= kappa, lift L.card <= lift kappa, lift #M <= lift kappa, then existential N.
hypotheses: Infinite M; aleph_0 <= kappa; Cardinal.lift.{w} L.card <= Cardinal.lift.{max u v} kappa; Cardinal.lift.{w} #M <= Cardinal.lift.{w'} kappa.
conclusion: There exists a bundled L-structure N with M elementarily equivalent to N and #N = kappa.

alternate_encodings.target: exists N, Nonempty (M ↪ₑ[L] N) and #N = kappa

excluded_degenerate_cases: Finite source structures; target cardinals below the required bounds; a merely equicardinal type without an L-structure; or a model with no checked elementary relationship to M.
